candidates.title: Boots: three brand positionings in five years ('Feel good' -> 'With you. For life.' -> 'Give it some Boots')
candidates.claim: Boots has had three positionings in five years under three CMOs; the old 'Feel good' line is still on a store window; Nike 'Just do it' (1988), Red Bull 'Gives you wings' (1987), L'Oreal 'You're worth it' (1971) cited as consistent exceptions. Opinion piece, no data.
candidates.note: Strongest universal tension: owners get bored of their brand long before customers learn it. Concrete image: old slogan still on the window while a new one is on TV.

candidates.title: Coca-Cola CMO questions 'brand love'
candidates.claim: Feature asks whether brand love drives results after Coca-Cola's CMO questioned it.
candidates.note: Fresh, but the CMO's exact words were not verified (homepage summary only, paywalled). Do not use as a claim.

candidates.title: Paramount + Warner Bros. Discovery to be named Skydance
candidates.claim: Combined company named after the least-known brand in the group; Warner Bros, HBO, DC, CNN keep identities; analyst calls it 'ego-driven'; uses existing Skydance Media logo.
candidates.note: Corporate vs consumer brand. Interesting, but customers never meet a holding name; weaker lesson for small business; political/ownership noise.

candidates.title: 'Does brand design have a longevity problem?' (Bud Rodecker)
candidates.claim: Hype-driven rebrands waste accumulated equity; build enduring systems.
candidates.note: Same idea as C01 from the design side; supports the chosen angle, but original not opened.

lenses_summary.verification_red_team: C01 is an opinion column with no data: treat 'three positionings in five years' and the slogans as reported facts (dates/names from Marketing Week and Retail Gazette); do NOT invent wear-out statistics (no 'consumers need X exposures' numbers). Nike 1988 confirmed by NPR/Dezeen; Red Bull 1987 and L'Oreal 1971 are as cited by Marketing Week only. Do not claim Boots' new platform is failing; no sales data. C06/C07/C09 headline-only, so excluded from claims.
lenses_summary.audience_psychology: Every owner has felt 'our logo/slogan is stale' — the reel names that itch and flips it: the fatigue is internal, the audience is barely starting to remember. Self-recognition is high; gentle sting, then relief (you do not need to change, you need to repeat).
lenses_summary.brand_fit: Fits Behnood's strategist voice: a contrarian, practical rule (refresh, don't restart). Works for Persian and English audiences without geography; Boots is only the spark, Nike/L'Oreal the proof. Avoids repeating 10-24 (that was visual codes of a pack; this is message/positioning consistency and the internal-boredom bias).

story.C01: tension: 'You are bored of your slogan; your customers have barely learned it.' image: an old slogan sticker still on the shop window while the new one plays on TV — three slogans layered on one glass.
story.C02: tension ok, image weak (a holding-company name customers never see)

decision.chosen: C01 (supported by C11 idea, C04 as contrast)
decision.why: Highest total (estimates), passes both gates, strongest universal tension and a concrete image, works natively in Persian and English, evergreen idea with a recent spark; not a repeat of the last 7 days.
